title: Context continued: portfolios, one long conversation, and compaction

beats.label: A folder of text files
beats.cue: The portfolio is a literal folder of Markdown text files.

beats.label: Open identity.md
beats.cue: Open identity.md to show ordinary text. The sample details are fictional.

beats.label: One portfolio, four rooms
beats.cue: The same human, four different agents and settings. One source portfolio remains on the monitor.

beats.label: Share the first five files
beats.cue: Each room receives its own copies of communication style, projects, decisions, domain knowledge, and goals.

beats.label: The same complete portfolio in every room
beats.cue: Identity, responsibilities, relationships, systems, and preferences complete all four matching portfolios. These are separate conversations, not shared live context.

beats.label: Return to our classroom
beats.cue: Whichever agent you choose, reading the files still takes up room in that conversation’s context window.

beats.label: Look closely at the context
beats.cue: Move closer to the classroom’s existing stacks. All ten topics remain where they landed.

beats.label: See the space it occupies
beats.cue: The portfolio takes space, but plenty remains. Hold here for the next part of the narration.

beats.section: Keep the portfolio up to date
beats.label: A new account and supporting team
beats.cue: A new fiscal year brings a new account and team. The user asks their agent to maintain the portfolio.

beats.section: Keep the portfolio up to date
beats.label: Update identity.md
beats.cue: Identity retains Alex’s name and role, and updates the account.

beats.section: Keep the portfolio up to date
beats.label: Update current-projects.md
beats.cue: Current projects reflects the new account and supporting team.

beats.section: Keep the portfolio up to date
beats.label: Update goals-and-priorities.md
beats.cue: Goals and priorities now point to supporting The Industrial Nugget Factory.

beats.section: Keep the portfolio up to date
beats.label: Update team-and-relationships.md
beats.cue: Team and relationships records Jack Sparrow, Ted Lasso, and David Beckham with the exact supplied roles.

beats.section: Keep the portfolio up to date
beats.label: Update role-and-responsibilities.md
beats.cue: Role and responsibilities reflects coordination with the new account team.

beats.section: Keep the portfolio up to date
beats.label: Updated context in our classroom
beats.cue: Five existing context boxes now carry a green revision seal. The other five are unchanged.

beats.section: Keep the portfolio up to date
beats.label: Save the five files to the computer
beats.cue: The five revised Markdown files are saved to the portfolio folder on the computer.

beats.section: Keep the portfolio up to date
beats.label: The saved portfolio is ready to reuse
beats.cue: The classroom has the new information. The other three rooms still have their earlier copies.

beats.section: Keep the portfolio up to date
beats.label: Other agents load the revised files
beats.cue: The other agents now read the revised files and refresh their own context. Saving a file alone does not refresh an already-running conversation. Existing boxes update in place; no extra tower is added.

beats.label: Stay in one conversation
beats.cue: Return to the classroom with the updated portfolio already present.

beats.label: Everything goes into this chat
beats.cue: One continuing conversation carries many different work topics. No new chat or context window is created.

beats.label: Fast-forward through weeks of work
beats.cue: Only this montage is fast-forwarded: account work, MCP tools, calls and results, writing, research, debugging, and personal tangents accumulate. The VHS effect stops before the hold.

beats.label: A costly quick question
beats.cue: Expense comes first in the narration: money flies out of the user’s pocket as another turn uses the long conversation. This is a playful metaphor, not a price estimate.

beats.label: Ask about an earlier decision
beats.cue: The user asks for the pilot success measures discussed with Ted at the beginning of the montage.

beats.label: Search the first aisle
beats.cue: Normal speed. The agent follows the right-hand gap, then the first narrow aisle. The first stack is a meal plan.

beats.label: Work around another stack
beats.cue: Normal speed. The agent goes around the left end of the next row and searches another aisle. This stack is espresso experiments.

beats.label: Find the earlier pilot decision
beats.cue: Normal speed. The agent reaches the back aisle and finds the original pilot goals: less manual follow-up and faster handoffs. The crowding makes the search harder; the information still exists here.

beats.label: Enter the context compactor
beats.cue: After the search, introduce compaction with a cartoon homage to the original Star Wars trash-compactor scene. Forty-nine individually rendered cartons and the armor represent the accumulated context in a shallow press bed.

beats.label: Crush the crowded context
beats.cue: The pressure walls ratchet inward. Outer cartons move only when a wall reaches them, then push their neighbors; touching cartons buckle separately, while a bracing pipe springs away. An abandoned stormtrooper helmet and chest plate are caught in the pile and crushed along with it.

beats.label: Stamp a summary cube
beats.cue: An overhead hydraulic press contacts the tallest stacks first, then compresses the supported cartons into a cube. The same cartons and armor remain in place when the press and walls reopen; there is no replacement cube. The cube is marked SUMMARY. This represents summarization, not lossless storage compression; details and instructions can be lost.
